sentences.text: 2. These two appeals are preferred under Section 16 of the Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishments Act, 2004 ('KPIDFE Act' for short), challenging the order passed by the learned Sessions Judge rejecting the prayer for anticipatory bail.

entities.text: Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. Crl.A.No.707/2023 arises out of Crl.Misc.No.125/2023 and Crl.A.No.723/2023 arises out of Crl.Misc.No.120/2023, both dated 03.03.2023.

4. Crime No.133/2022 of Nanjangud Police Station, Mysuru District, was registered on a complaint lodged by one Sri Prakash H.M., against the appellant for the offences punishable under Sections 403, 406 and 420 of the IPC and Section 9 of the KPIDFE Act.

It is alleged that one M Shambulingu,
husband of the appellant insisted the first informant to open an account in a chit being run in the name of his wife/appellant and on his insistence, he joined in two chits NC: 2024:KHC:10816 C/W CRL.A NO.723 of 2023 and deposited a total sum of Rs.5,20,000/.
But on maturity, said amount was not returned, despite the assurance given.
It is alleged that similarly the accused has cheated several other depositors to the tune of lakhs of rupees.

5. Cr.No.138/2022 of Nanjangud Town Police Station, Mysuru was registered on a complaint lodged by one Mallappa B Hadli against accused Nos.1 to 3 for the offences punishable under Sections 403,
406, 420 and 114 of IPC and Section 9 of the KPIDFE Act.

It is alleged that the appellant's husband namely, M Shambulingu, insisted the first informant to join the chit which was run in the name of the appellant and on his insistence, the first informant opened two accounts and deposited a total sum of Rs.7,20,000/-.

However, on maturity the accused did not return the deposited amount and thereby cheated him etc.
6.

It is further alleged that accused Nos.2 and 3 namely, father and brother of the appellant colluded with each other and purchased properties out of the proceeds collected from several persons and cheated them etc.

7. Learned High Court Government Pleader has contended that the chit was run in the name of the appellant NC: 2024:KHC:10816 C/W CRL.A NO.723 of 2023 and in collusion with each other,
accused have collected huge amount from the complainants and others by inducing them to join the chit and thereafter, failed to return the amount.
He has contended that the leaned Sessions Judge has rightly rejected the prayer seeking anticipatory bail in view of bar under Section 18(2) of the KPIDFE Act.

8. The learned Sessions Judge has rejected the prayer seeking anticipatory bail relying on the decision of this Court in Shreesha Sasithota Pabhakaan Vs. The State of Karnataka (Crl.P.No.9971/2022 (D.D.10.11.2022) and further observing that petition under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. or 439 of Cr.P.C. is not maintainable when the offences under the KPIDFE Act are incorporated and the only remedy available is to file an appeal under Section 16 of that Act.

sentences.text: One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is that Section 9 of the KPIDFE Act is not applicable to the case on hand, since the definition of 'deposit' does not include the amount received by way of subscription in respect of a chit.
He has therefore contended that there is no prima-facie case made out for the offences alleged to have been committed under the KPIDFE Act.
As per the definition of 'deposit' under Section 2(2)(vii) of the KPIDFE Act, 'deposit' does not include amount received by way of subscriptions in respect of chit.

The offence alleged under the said Act is one under Section 9 i.e., any financial establishment fraudulently committing default in repayment of deposit etc., hence at this stage, it cannot be said that prima facie case is made out against the appellant for the said offence.

11. It is the case of prosecution that the appellant's husband who was working as a High School teacher induced the complainant and similar other persons to join the chit which was run in the name of his wife i.e., the appellant and thereafter, failed to return the deposited amount and thereby cheated them etc.

The appellant's husband committed suicide and on coming to know about the same, when the complainant approached the appellant requesting her to return the amount, it is alleged that she failed to return the amount inspite of the assurances given by her and colluded with accused Nos.2 and 3 and invested the amount collected from various persons in properties.
The prosecution has to establish its case in due course.
The offences alleged are not punishable with death or imprisonment for life.
The appellant is a woman.
This Court by its order dated 18.04.2023 has granted interim bail to the appellant in both the cases.

It is submitted by the learned counsel that pursuant to the said order, the appellant has appeared before the Investigating Officer and executed the bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- with a surety for the likesum and she has been co-operating with the investigation of the case.

13. In the above facts and circumstances, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The Criminal appeals are allowed.

The impugned order dated 03.03.2023 p a s s e d b y t h e P r i n c i p a l D i s t r i c t & S e s s i o n s J u d g e , a t M y s u r u , i n Crl.Misc.No.125/2023 and Crl.Misc.No.120/2023 are set-aside.

The interim bail granted by this Court on 18.04.2023 to the appellant in these appeals is made absolute with further conditions as under:
NC: 2024:KHC:10816 C/W CRL.A NO.723 of 2023 i) The appellant shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required for the purpose of investigation.
